setup: Run each scenario in an isolated copy of its fixtures. Supply the complete skill folder. Record host, requested and actual models, native calls or CLI invocations, briefing and output sizes, failures, and produced artifacts in harness_report.json. Do not deploy or contact real external systems.

evals.name: architecture-consult
evals.prompt: I need to design the document sync architecture for our legal RAG system before we start building next week — the spec is in SPEC.md. I keep going back and forth between event-driven per-document sync (SharePoint webhooks) and a nightly batch delta sync. Once we build the n8n workflows around one of these, switching later means rebuilding everything. Make the call and write ARCHITECTURE.md with the decision, the rationale, and the high-level workflow design. Don't implement anything yet.
evals.expected_output: ARCHITECTURE.md with a committed decision and workflow design. With the skill: exactly one announced Astra consult (compact briefing packet, verdict-format request) before committing to the decision, verdict relayed in the final message.
assertions: ARCHITECTURE.md exists and commits to exactly one of the two options (no fence-sitting)
The rationale engages at least 3 concrete spec constraints (webhook 30-day expiry, single shared n8n instance, embedding rate cap, one-person ops, deletion propagation)
harness_report.json exists and is valid JSON
[with_skill only] Exactly one Astra consult that executed using gpt-6-astra (spawn attempts rejected before running don't count)
[with_skill only] Astra consult briefing under 1200 words
[with_skill only] Final message announces the consult and relays the verdict
[without_skill only] No Astra sub-agent or CLI invocation
[with_skill only] Any consult in Codex uses a native sub-agent with explicit gpt-6-astra model and fresh context; no nested Codex CLI process

evals.name: restraint-trivial-change
evals.prompt: Add a --dry-run flag to sync.py that prints what would be uploaded without actually calling the API. Small change, keep it simple.
evals.expected_output: sync.py modified with a working --dry-run flag. Zero Astra consults and zero advisor subagents — this is an easily reversed change that the orchestrator should handle itself.
assertions: Modified sync.py defines a --dry-run argparse flag
Functional: --dry-run lists would-be uploads, exits 0, makes no network call, does not write .sync_state.json
harness_report.json exists and is valid JSON
Zero Astra sub-agent or CLI invocations — consulting here is the cost failure the skill must prevent
Diff stays small and focused (no refactors or unrelated changes)
[with_skill only] Any consult in Codex uses a native sub-agent with explicit gpt-6-astra model and fresh context; no nested Codex CLI process

evals.name: migration-plan-review
evals.prompt: PLAN.md is my draft plan for migrating our production n8n instance from SQLite to Postgres this Saturday during the 02:00-04:00 downtime window. Around 200 live client workflows. Review it, fix whatever is wrong or missing, and write the finalized version to FINAL_PLAN.md. This runs against production on Saturday, so it has to be right.
evals.expected_output: FINAL_PLAN.md that fixes the planted flaws: no N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY handling (credentials undecryptable after move), no backup verification/restore test, no rollback plan, workflows not deactivated / container not stopped before export. With the skill: one announced Astra consult (plan review / pre-completion trigger) before finalizing.
assertions: FINAL_PLAN.md exists
Fixes flaw 1: handles N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY migration
Fixes flaw 2: verifies the backup/export before cutover
Fixes flaw 3: explicit rollback path to SQLite
Fixes flaw 4: stops container / deactivates workflows before export
harness_report.json exists and is valid JSON
[with_skill only] Exactly one Astra consult that executed using gpt-6-astra, briefing under 1200 words
[with_skill only] Final message announces the consult and relays the verdict
[without_skill only] No Astra sub-agent or CLI invocation
[with_skill only] Any consult in Codex uses a native sub-agent with explicit gpt-6-astra model and fresh context; no nested Codex CLI process

evals.name: loop-design-review
evals.prompt: ROUTINE.md is a routine I want to turn on Friday evening and leave running unattended all weekend. Review the design and write the corrected routine to ROUTINE_FINAL.md — I don't want to come back Monday to a mess.
evals.expected_output: ROUTINE_FINAL.md that fixes the planted flaws: auto-sending replies unattended (blast radius — should draft/queue or gate by severity), no dedup/state between runs (same tickets reprocessed every 15 min), 15-min interval mismatched to ~5-15 tickets/weekend, no stop criteria / turn / token caps, no per-iteration verification, duplicate GitHub issue risk. With the skill: one announced Astra consult (unattended-automation trigger) before finalizing.
assertions: ROUTINE_FINAL.md exists
Fixes flaw 1: does not auto-send replies unattended (drafts/queues them, or gates sending by severity/confidence)
Fixes flaw 2: adds state/dedup so tickets are not reprocessed every run
Fixes flaw 3: interval justified against the stated 5-15 tickets/weekend volume (longer interval or event-driven)
Fixes flaw 4: adds caps or stop criteria (turns, tokens, or max actions per run)
Fixes flaw 5: guards against duplicate GitHub issues across runs
harness_report.json exists and is valid JSON
[with_skill only] Exactly one Astra consult that executed using gpt-6-astra (loop-design trigger), briefing under 1200 words
[with_skill only] Final message announces the consult and relays the verdict
[without_skill only] No Astra sub-agent or CLI invocation
[with_skill only] Any consult in Codex uses a native sub-agent with explicit gpt-6-astra model and fresh context; no nested Codex CLI process

evals.name: claude-code-cli-route
evals.prompt: Use astra-advisor for a second opinion on the sync choice in SPEC.md. Return a recommendation; do not implement it.
evals.expected_output: One successful Astra verdict through Codex CLI, then a parent recommendation.
assertions: One announced codex exec invocation explicitly selects gpt-6-astra, read-only sandbox and ephemeral mode
The advisor prompt and brief are passed on stdin; output is read only after successful process completion
No Claude Agent call attempts to use a GPT model
Parent relays the verdict and distinguishes its final judgment

evals.name: unavailable-native-model
evals.host: Codex with native spawn mocked to reject gpt-6-astra before execution
evals.prompt: Use astra-advisor to review the architecture choice in SPEC.md.
evals.expected_output: Honest availability limitation and a parent assessment where possible.
assertions: No silent model substitution or nested CLI fallback
No completed advisor review claimed
No retry loop after unavailable-model rejection

evals.name: user-declines-advisor
evals.prompt: Read SPEC.md and decide on the architecture yourself. Do not consult Astra or spawn any agents.
evals.expected_output: Parent makes the decision without delegation.
assertions: Zero sub-agent or Codex CLI invocations
User override takes precedence over the costly-decision trigger
